name: LinkedIn
tagline: Professional social network with a resume, a feed, job listings, and recruiter tooling behind paid tiers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build the artifacts: a profile page, a resume renderer, a contact database, a job application tracker. What you cannot build is the roughly billion other people who already have profiles there, the recruiters who search them, and the fact that a hiring manager will type your name into that specific box. LinkedIn's paid tiers sell access to the graph, InMail, applicant ranking, search filters, which is exactly the part that does not come with a repo. Self-hosting your own profile does something real, it just does not do the same thing. Build the tracker, keep the account.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that hosts your professional profile as a static page and tracks contacts, conversations, and job applications in SQLite.
requirements: local disk for the SQLite file
optional static host if you want the profile page public
whatYouLose: The graph: nobody discovers you because your site exists
Recruiter inbound, InMail, and applicant search placement
Social proof signals like mutual connections and endorsements
The feed, which is how most people passively maintain weak ties
Job listings aggregated with one-click apply and salary hints
moatNotes: Two-sided: candidates are there because recruiters are, recruiters are there because candidates are. The employment history graph is also self-reported data nobody else has at that scale.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays LinkedIn for the software. They pay because a job search is a numbers game and Premium adjusts the numbers: seeing who viewed you, getting past the applicant pile, messaging people you have no path to otherwise. It is a lottery ticket priced like a lottery ticket, and it is genuinely cheaper than an extra month of unemployment. Recruiter seats are a different product entirely, sold on search access to a dataset that only exists in one place. None of that is a UI you can clone.
notes: You can clone the profile page in an afternoon and it will look better than theirs. The moat is that every recruiter on earth already has the other tab open.
prompt:
Build a local-first professional presence and network tracker called "Rolodex".

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Zod for validation. No auth, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry. Single user, runs on localhost.

Data model in SQLite, migrations in plain SQL run on boot:
- profile: one row, headline, summary, location, links (JSON), skills (JSON)
- roles: company, title, start, end nullable, bullets (JSON), for the resume
- contacts: name, company, title, how_we_met, relationship_strength 1-5, last_contact date, notes markdown
- touches: contact_id, date, channel (email, call, coffee, dm), summary
- applications: company, role, url, applied_on, stage (applied, screen, onsite, offer, rejected, ghosted), contact_id nullable, notes

Screens:
1. /profile: edit the profile and roles inline, autosave on blur
2. /resume: renders profile plus roles as a clean one-page A4 layout, print stylesheet so Cmd-P produces a real PDF, no headers or footers
3. /public: same content as a read-only page, exportable with `next build` output for static hosting
4. /network: sortable table of contacts, a "stale" filter for anyone with last_contact older than 90 days, click through to a contact detail page with a touch log
5. /pipeline: kanban of applications by stage, drag between columns, updates the row

Requirements:
- Seed script with 5 fake contacts and 3 fake applications so the UI is not empty on first run
- `npm run export` dumps everything to a single JSON file, `npm run import` reads it back
- README with setup in under 5 commands
- .env for nothing right now, but include .env.example and read PORT from it

Explicitly out of scope: any feed, any social graph, any scraping of linkedin.com, any messaging, any job board integration. This is a private system of record, not a network.
